data.name: DYING: Reborn
data.detailed_description:
“DYING: Reborn” é um jogo de primeira pessoa onde o jogador deve resolver uma série de quebra-cabeças em um Escape Room de terror.



O personagem principal, Mathew, acorda em um hotel abandonado, sombrio e assustador, e é contatado por um personagem misterioso que explica que ele deverá passar por uma série de testes devido a um grave erro cometido no passado. O jogo possui 6 capítulos no total, e caso Mathew não passe nestes testes, pagará um alto preço.



- Busque por objetos e interaja com tudo em um ambiente 3D, usando sua imaginação e inteligência para resolver mistérios.

- Apenas encontrando e investigando as pistas você conseguirá decifrar o mistério do passado de Mathew.



- Nos 6 capítulos do jogo você encontrará personagens misteriosos e verá coisas bizarras.

- Use o seu cérebro para resolver uma série de quebra-cabeças desafiadores.

- É preciso coragem para enfrentar este cenário de filme de terror.

reviews.review:
[h1] This Game Fails As A Horror Game, And As An Escape Room Game [/h1]

(By the way, I've beaten this game on my VITA. I only bought the PC version to see what's different and such, but sadly, while the PC version has extra things, it's not all that different from the VITA release. So the 0.8 hours I have with the PC version, I knew what to do most of the time, and made it to room 4 fast.)

DYING: Reborn is an escape room "horror" game where you Mathew, who's trying to find his sister when he received a letter from her. While Mathew visits a town in Harbour City, but then he gets captured and wakes up in the middle of a room. Your job is to solve puzzles, find Mathew's sister, and figure out what's going on.

This story is really flawed and poorly written. There's a good amount of questions that aren't answered (or plot holes), the ending is pretty predictable, and the characters aren't likable. Mathew is pretty damn annoying, he always whines, and he says some pretty questionable stuff at times. His sister doesn't get any character development. The lady in the TV also doesn't get much character development. The main villain is the most likable, but that doesn't mean he's a good characters, just interesting enough. There are moments where the game tries to be paranormal-ish, and doesn't make any sense (Like a Mannequin that smashed through glass, even though nobody threw it.). The story fails hard here.

The gameplay isn't good either. When it comes to puzzles, they're really easy, with one or two where you need to be in the developer's mind in order to solve the puzzle (I, and other had to look up a guide due to those puzzles making zero sense). The controls are good, they make the game playable. You can use items you find to solve puzzles or get through obstacles, make progress. You can click on pictures or other things to put into your Memo, which is useful if the pictures or something is important. Other things though, at times they're just for small parts of the story, but they're nothing worth while. To be honest, there's not really much on what to say about the gameplay of this game, but when it comes to the horror aspect, this is where it fails hard. It's only just jumpscares that are predictable, and low quality sounds.

Speaking of sound, the sound choices/design and voice acting are horrendous. The voice acting is Resident Evil 1 levels of voice acting. Mathew and the other characters sound like they're bored, resulting in such dull performances. The only decent voice actor in this game is the main villain, but that's it. The sound choices/design goes from a girl's scream getting caught off at the end, to low quality music in the loading menus (well, the music was low quality on my PC at least). Hell, the sound of opening up your inventory is surround sound, which means if you're looking in a direction, there's a chance sound effects in the inventory will only happen in one of your ears, until you look at a different direction to make it so that the sounds are in both ears. Not to mention, the music in this game is really forgettable. It's not bad, but it's nothing special.

The only okay thing about this game are the graphics. Nothing groundbreaking, but they get the job done.

Over and all, this game isn't worth your time. From the poorly written makes-no-sense story, to the poor characters, to boring gameplay, to horrendous sound effects and voice acting, to a poor ending as well. It's not the worst game I've ever played, hell I have a feeling the developers put a lot of effort into it, but for a room escape "horror" game, it's a pretty bad one. There are better room escape games out there.

[h1] FINAL SCORE: 2/10 [/h1]

[i] If you like this game, good for you! We all have opinions. [/i]
